govdocs-archive_org-WOIlluminatiFreemaso: Helen Peters’s The Union Jack — from the WOIlluminatiFreemasons archive — is a fragment on secret societies. The file’s full context is unclear. Archivists value such fragments. Its claims should be read critically. The item is a curiosity of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAWatergate_CI: This item — CIA Watergate — is a National Security Internet Archive file on the CIA’s Watergate role. The file’s full context is unclear. The scandal reached the agency’s doorstep. Researchers value such files. The item is a fragment of the intelligence archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ClarkWilliamKem: These notes on the deposition of Dr. William Kemp Clark — creator unknown — are a file on the Parkland doctor. Parkland doctors fought to save the president. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DeathCertificat: This G-man memo — asks about copies of JFK’s death paper — is a Bureau file. The opened memo is a first-hand source. Even the death paper drew hard looks. Bookmen prize such files. The file fits the JFK-killing shelf.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FOIAPrivacyActR: Bert Andrews’s Washington Hunt excerpt is a press file on the capital’s scandals. Andrews covered Washington for decades. The excerpt is a teaser. The full work awaits. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HollywoodReport: Jay Carr’s Stone Defends JFK: ‘I’ve Done All My Homework’ covers Oliver Stone’s film. The 1991 film reignited the debate. Stone stood his ground. The film won Oscars. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-IntelligenceAge: William Greider’s Again, Government Claims the Power to Snoop covers surveillance overreach. Greider was a sharp critic of power. The piece warned readers. The snooping continued. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
myths-and-legends-of-our-own-land-comple: This complete edition gathers all of Charles Skinner's volumes of American folklore in one place — from Hudson ghosts to Pacific treasure tales. Hundreds of legends cover every region of the country, making it the fullest single collection of its kind. For storytellers, historians, and the simply curious, it is an inexhaustible American storybook.
the-log-of-the-empire-state: Geneve Shaffer keeps the log of a voyage aboard the Empire State — day by day, port by port, with a traveler's eye for people and places. Shipboard life, strange shores, and fellow passengers fill an engaging narrative. A pleasant companion for readers who love the romance of sea travel.
the-adventures-of-ferdinand-count-fathom: This complete edition gathers Smollett's full portrait of Ferdinand Count Fathom, from his scheming youth to his comeuppance. The novel's unflinching look at a thorough villain shocked some readers and fascinated others. A cornerstone of the English novel, in one volume at last.
the-heart-of-mid-lothian-complete: The complete Heart of Mid-Lothian gathers Jeanie Deans's whole heroic journey — from Edinburgh's Tolbooth to her pilgrimage to London for royal mercy. Scott's most tender and moral novel, in one volume. A masterpiece of the Waverley series. No reader finishes Jeanie's journey unchanged by her quiet, unshakeable goodness.
old-mortality-complete: Scott's complete Old Mortality presents the full tragedy of Scotland's Killing Time — Covenanters against dragoons, faith against the sword. Henry Morton's story remains one of historical fiction's great achievements. The Waverley Novel in its complete and terrible power. Few historical novels have matched its sweep, its sympathy, and its terrible beauty.
telling-fortunes-by-tea-leaves-how-to-re: Cicely Kent reveals the traditional art of reading tea leaves — the symbols, the ritual, the interpretation of what the cup foretells. Part folklore, part parlor game, her guide preserves a charming divination tradition. For the curious, the playful, and the romantic at heart.
the-antiquary-complete: Scott's complete Antiquary gathers Jonathan Oldbuck's whole story — the buried treasure, the lost heir restored, and the noble beggar Edie Ochiltree. Considered by many his most perfectly constructed novel, it blends humor, mystery, and deep humanity. Scottish life and character at their finest.
rob-roy-complete: The whole of Scott's Rob Roy in one volume — Frank's northern journey, Rob Roy's daring, and Diana Vernon's charm, from first page to last. Many call it the finest of the Waverley Novels' adventures. Highland romance at its most stirring.
the-yosemite: John Muir, the great prophet of the wilderness, pours his love for Yosemite into these glowing pages. Granite cliffs, waterfalls, and giant sequoias live in prose that helped save the valley for the nation. The book that made Yosemite a household word.
the-great-conspiracy-complete: The complete Great Conspiracy gathers General Logan's full history of the Civil War — from secession's roots to Appomattox — in one work. A Union hero's partisan, powerful account of the nation's trial. Essential for students of the conflict. Seven volumes bound as one give the whole sweep of the war from a Union hero's unblinking view.
afghanistan-and-the-anglo-russian-disput: Theophilus Rodenbough, an old soldier, weighs the fight over Afghanistan — Britain and Russia glaring at each other across the passes. His plain, shrewd pages light up the Great Game that shaped empires. Still worth reading for all who would grasp that hard land.
the-early-life-of-mark-rutherford-w-hale: William Hale White recalls his early life as Mark Rutherford — dissenting chapels, bookshops, and the making of a writer. His plain memoir is deeply moving. The roots of a singular genius. Chapel pews and printing offices formed the rebel thinker to come.
the-poetical-works-of-oliver-wendell-hol: The complete Holmes in one volume — from Old Ironsides to the last teacup poems, the whole bright career of Boston's Autocrat. Doctor, wit, and patriot, he was among America's best-loved voices. An essential classic for every American shelf. Here is a lifetime of wit and warmth between two covers.
dryden-s-palamon-and-arcite: Dryden's Palamon and Arcite — his splendid retelling of Chaucer's Knight's Tale — glows in heroic couplets. Two noble friends, one fair lady, and a tournament decide their fate. The great Augustan poet at his narrative best. Emily's beauty sets the noblest friendship ever sung at strife.
a-book-of-old-ballads-complete: The complete Book of Old Ballads — all four volumes in one — gives England's ballad heritage whole and undivided. From Robin Hood to Chevy Chase, every favorite finds its place. The definitive Nichols collection for ballad lovers. No better door into old England's poetry exists.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-miri: The Encyclopedia's brief entry on the abbey of the Miridites, in the Albanian hills. Mountain Christians kept the faith there. Anthony Gancevic notes its place. A far-flung outpost of the old Church. Few travelers ever reach its mountain solitude.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acolyte: A 1913 entry on the acolyte — the minor order that serves the altar. Andrew Meehan describes his duties. Candle, cruets, and bells are his charge. The Church's youngest ministers. He lights the candles and pours the wine. Many a priest began at this step.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acquapendente: This 1913 reference article on Acquapendente — the Tuscan diocese of the hanging waters. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its cathedral keeps an ancient relic. A hill town's church history. Its Holy Sepulchre relic draws pilgrims. The Via Francigena passed its gates.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adoro-te-devo: A 1913 entry on Adoro Te Devote — St. Thomas' hidden-God hymn to the Eucharist. Hugh Henry unfolds its seven stanzas. Godhead here in hiding, whom I adore. Every Benediction sings it still. The Angelic Doctor's tenderest verse. Its melody lifts hearts every Benediction.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adrien-rouque: A 1913 entry on Abbé Adrien Rouquette — the Louisiana priest-poet of the Choctaws. Susan Blanchard Elder celebrates his verse. He lived among his Indian flock. His poems sang the bayou wilds. The apostle of the Choctaws. His Choctaw grammar aided the missionaries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alberico-de-r: This 1913 reference piece on Alberico de Rosate — the great jurist of Bergamo. Johann Peter Kirsch praises his legal works. His dictionary guided lawyers for centuries. The schools called him doctor. A prince of the civilians. His works filled the lawyers' libraries.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-berrug: This 1913 reference piece on Alonso Berruguete — Spain's great carver of the Renaissance — praises his work. Augustus Van Cleef follows his career. His saints twist with holy fire. Toledo's choir stalls show his best. His tomb effigies are Valladolid's pride. The Spanish master of the chisel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrosian-lit: A 1913 entry on the Ambrosian liturgy and rite — Milan's ancient Mass. Henry Jenner explains its venerable forms. Charlemagne could not suppress it. The Duomo keeps its yearly round. The West's surviving local rite. Its Mass is longer than Rome's. Its Advent has six Sundays.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrew-white: A 1913 entry on Andrew White — the Jesuit apostle of Maryland. Edward Devitt honors his mission. His Ark and Dove brought the faith. The Calverts trusted his counsel. The founder of the Maryland mission. His Relatio told the mission's tale. His chapel stood on St. Clement's isle.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antofogaste: This 1913 reference piece on Antofagasta — the Chilean desert diocese. The entry tells its nitrate story. Its churches serve the mining ports. The Atacama yields its wealth. A bishopric of the northern desert. Its cathedral faces the Pacific surf. Its mines built the desert city.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-appetite: This 1913 reference article on appetite in philosophy — the soul's reaching for the good. Charles Dubray treats it scholastically. The will follows the known good. The passions serve or rebel. The engine of the moral life. Its schooling is the ascetic's art.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aquileian-rit: This 1913 reference piece on the Aquileian rite — the old liturgy of the patriarchate. Adrian Fortescue unfolds its venerable form. The north Adriatic prayed its own Mass. The Roman rite at last prevailed. A vanished liturgy of the north. Its chant differed from Rome's.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archimandrite: This 1913 reference piece on the archimandrite — the Eastern abbot. Andrew Shipman explains his honored rank. He rules the monastery or district. The title crowns the monastic chief. The East's father superior. His staff marks the monastic rank. His rank precedes the simple abbot.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedict-welt: This 1913 reference article on Benedict Welte — a theologian of note. John Fox records his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. His pen served the Tübingen schools. A teacher of the sacred science. His lectures drew the Tübingen students.
